subject: PrivCP role provisioning connector design
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@telcocloud.com>

Cc: idp-integration@telcocloud.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivCP role provisioning connector - initial scope

Hi Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this on. TelcoCloud is preparing a VPC private control plane deployment and we need to settle on how roles and entitlements will be provisioned from our IdP into Redwood's Private Control Plane. High level asks: 

- We want SCIM-based provisioning for user accounts + group-to-role mapping.
- SAML assertions will carry role hints during SSO.
- We need a durable audit trail (who provisioned which role and when) for SOC 2.

Attached is a rough role matrix and a short list of attributes we currently emit. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports group->role mapping at the resource scope (project/org) and how we should structure SCIM groups?

Proposed session to align: next Tue/Thu morning PT.

Laura
Identity Ops — TelcoCloud

Attachments: role-matrix-v1.xlsx
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@telcocloud.com>, idp-integration@telcocloud.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivCP role provisioning connector - initial scope

Laura —

Thanks, got the matrix. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, Private Control Plane supports SCIM v2 provisioning. We map SCIM groups to PrivCP roles via a configurable role-mapping table; groups can be scoped to org or project using a naming convention (e.g., redwood:org:ID:role and redwood:proj:ID:role).
- SAML assertions: we accept an optional 'roles' attribute and also look for 'groups' in the assertion; if both are present we reconcile by union with precedence rules configurable per customer.
- Audit trail: provisioning operations are logged to the private control plane audit log. We can export logs to your SIEM over TLS and retain them per your retention policy.

Two questions before the alignment call:
1) Do you want group names to be canonicalized (we support mapping rules) or will TelcoCloud supply the canonical form?
2) Any constraints on SCIM PATCH frequency? Some IdPs send frequent deltas — we recommend a 60s dedupe window for high-throughput directories.

I'll schedule a 1-hour sync for Tue 10/10 PT (propose 10:00 PT) and loop in Platform IAM (Rishi) for the role precedence discussion.

—Sean
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@telcocloud.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: idp-integration@telcocloud.com, Andy Park <andy.park@atlantech.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivCP role provisioning connector - initial scope

Sean —

Answers inline:

1) We'll supply group names from our provisioning directory but prefer to use TelcoCloud canonical names (we already have naming policies). Would like Redwood to accept mapping rules in case we need to rename on our side.
2) We expect frequent deltas; 60s dedupe is fine but can you confirm support for bulk replace vs PATCH semantics (we prefer replace semantics for groups).

Andy from Atlantech (our integration partner) is on copy to weigh in on connector patterns — they build SCIM connectors and have suggested a hybrid approach (initial full sync, then delta + periodic reconcile).

Attaching a short spec of SAML attributes we plan to emit.

Laura

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivCP role provisioning connector - initial scope

Thanks Laura — a few implementation notes from Platform IAM: 

- We recommend a default precedence: explicit SAML 'roles' attribute > SCIM group mapping > SAML 'groups' claim. This prevents accidental privilege escalation when an IdP sends both.
- Support for bulk 'replace' operation for group membership is available; our connector supports both PATCH (incremental) and full replace. For high-churn directories, use PATCH with page-size tuning to reduce reconciliation windows.
- Dedup window: configurable at install-time; 60s is a safe default. We also support a reconciliation job (daily/weekly) to fix drift.
- For audit requirements: we'll enable signed provisioning events (HMAC headers) and include a provisioning_request_id that your IdP can log. These provisioning_request_id values are surfaced in the control plane audit logs and can be exported.

I'll add a short YAML mapping template to the shared drive before the call.

—Rishi
Staff Engineer, Platform IAM
